features.name: Direct transact capability on appsource
features.description: ISVs can sell their add-on apps directly to end customers through appsource using credit card or Microsoft billing system. Customers can purchase apps immediately from the ISV.
caveats: Applicable to add-ons only, not connect apps

features.name: Three percent flat transaction fee
features.description: Microsoft charges ISVs a three percent flat transaction fee per transaction. This includes platform maintenance, Azure hosting on Business Central, money collection, and automatic deposit to ISV bank accounts.

features.name: Flexible pricing models support
features.description: ISVs can use various pricing models including per-user, per-company, one-time fee, custom meters like per pay slip or transaction, and combinations like tiered offerings with custom reading.

features.name: One catalog with multi-channel distribution
features.description: Microsoft maintains one central catalog containing all Microsoft SKUs and third-party ISV solutions. Solutions can be made available through appsource, in-product purchase, and the CSP reseller channel.

features.name: CSP channel enablement for ISV solutions
features.description: ISVs can distribute their solutions through the Cloud Solution Provider reseller channel in addition to direct appsource sales, enabling reach through a network of resellers.

features.name: Plan variations in offers
features.description: ISVs can create multiple plans within a single offer to represent variations such as feature tiers, waterfall pricing based on license quantities, or market-specific pricing differences.

features.name: In-product purchase experience
features.description: Solutions made available in the one catalog can be exposed through in-product purchase experiences within Business Central itself, enabling seamless discovery and acquisition.
caveats: Described as potential future experience

features.name: Sell Through Microsoft for AppSource Apps
features.description: Publishers can opt into selling their Business Central apps directly through Microsoft in AppSource. This requires creating plans and managing them through Partner Center with options for different pricing models and market-specific configurations.
caveats: Requires opt-in per app
Different from connect apps which use out-of-box APIs only

features.name: Country-Specific Plans
features.description: When opting into AppSource transactability, country-market setup moves from the offer level to the plan level, allowing publishers to create plans that are country-specific with different pricing per market.
caveats: Only applicable when opting into AppSource transactability

features.name: Waterfall Pricing Model
features.description: Publishers can structure plans using waterfall pricing, where customers receive discounts based on the number of licenses purchased in a single transaction. Plans can specify minimum and maximum user license amounts.
caveats: Alternative to functional tier-based plans

features.name: Billing Frequency Options
features.description: Publishers can offer both monthly and yearly billing cycles for their plans. Yearly subscriptions can include a discount option to incentivize longer-term commitments.

features.name: Trial Subscription Support
features.description: Publishers can offer free trials of their applications or plans. Trials are currently limited to one month duration, and customers must provide credit card information during the trial signup process.
caveats: Trial limited to one month
Requires credit card information
Automatically converts to paid subscription if not canceled

features.name: Private Plans
features.description: Publishers can make plans private so that only specific AAD tenants or inter-tenants can view them in AppSource. This enables custom pricing and tiering for specific customers while public plans are visible to everyone.
caveats: Private plans extend to specific AAD tenants

features.name: Automatic Currency Conversion for Plans
features.description: Partner Center automatically converts plan pricing from US dollars to local currencies based on current exchange rates for all defined markets. Publishers can also manually set prices for different countries and import custom pricing.
caveats: Default is automatic conversion
Publishers can export and manually set pricing per country

features.name: Buy Now Button for Apps
features.description: Apps opted into AppSource transactability display a Buy Now button in the AppSource listing, enabling customers to purchase and transact directly within AppSource without leaving the marketplace.

features.name: Plan and Pricing Tab in AppSource
features.description: AppSource listings for transactable apps display a new tab called Plans and Pricing where customers can view and compare different plan options, functional tiers, and pricing variations before purchasing.

features.name: Checkout Process for AppSource Apps
features.description: Customers can select a plan, choose monthly or yearly subscription with optional recurring billing, specify the number of licenses, and complete the purchase using a credit card. The checkout process guides customers through order review and billing information.
caveats: Requires credit card for purchase

features.name: License Assignment in Admin Center
features.description: After purchasing licenses through AppSource, customers must assign those licenses to users in the Microsoft Admin Center. The Admin Center shows product overview, license details, subscription information, and allows license assignment and cancellation.
caveats: Licenses are separate from app installation
App must be installed separately in Business Central environment

features.name: App Installation via Admin Center
features.description: Customers can install purchased apps in their Business Central environment from either AppSource or the Microsoft Admin Center. This is a separate step from license purchasing and assignment.
caveats: Separate action from license purchase and assignment

features.name: Combined Billing for Business Central Solutions
features.description: Customers receive a single combined invoice from Microsoft that includes both AppSource app licenses and first-party Business Central license costs, providing unified visibility into total solution expenses.

features.name: Publisher Insights in Partner Center
features.description: Partner Center provides publishers with analytics and insights about their AppSource apps, including order details, license revenue, customer count, and other business metrics to track sales performance.
caveats: Many more insights available beyond what was mentioned

features.name: Entitlements for AppSource Apps
features.description: Publishers must define entitlements in their apps that map licenses purchased through AppSource to Business Central permissions. Entitlements are configured with an ID matching the plan ID and specify object access permissions for users with that license.
caveats: Entitlements define maximum permissions
Admin must still grant permissions to users in Business Central
Required for any AppSource transactability

features.name: Entitlement Per-User Offer Plans
features.description: Entitlements are configured with type per-user offer plan, mapping the plan ID from Partner Center to permissions that users with that license have access to in Business Central. The entitlement specifies the maximum permission set available.
caveats: Admin must separately grant permissions in Business Central

features.name: Admin Permission Grant Requirement
features.description: Even though entitlements define the maximum permissions a user can access based on their license, the Business Central admin must explicitly grant those permissions to each user. A user can have a license but not actual access without admin permission assignment.
caveats: Two-step process required

features.name: Entitlements mapping
features.description: Entitlements map between licenses or roles that users have and the access they need in applications. They define the maximum permissions a user can access based on their assigned plan.
caveats: Admin must still grant specific user permissions; license does not auto-grant access
Admins in Business Central must grant users permissions even if they have the license

features.name: Group-based entitlements
features.description: Users can be entitled to permissions through membership in Azure AD groups. Developers can be given a group entitlement with different permissions than regular customers.

features.name: Unlicensed user entitlements
features.description: A special entitlement type that allows code to determine access for users without licenses based on custom licensing logic. Enables backward compatibility for existing customers migrating to platform licensing.
caveats: Requires custom code to determine access in application
Must check customer status via internal licensing logic or API

features.name: Administrator entitlements
features.description: Entitlements based on administrator roles allow local and delegated admins to access setup functionality without purchasing licenses. Supports Dynamics 365 administrator, internal administrator, and delegated admin roles.
caveats: Limited to specific administrator roles defined in system app

features.name: License-conditional functionality
features.description: Application code can check if users have specific Business Central licenses (premium, embed) using the is_entitled method to enable or disable features based on their license type.

features.name: CSP direct and indirect models
features.description: Two CSP purchasing models: direct (customer buys from partner, partner from Microsoft) and indirect (customer from reseller, reseller from indirect provider, provider from Microsoft).
caveats: Functionality available through Partner Center interface for CSP directs and indirect providers

features.name: Resale through CSP
features.description: ISVs can opt into selling apps through CSP partners in Partner Center. Can restrict sales to specific CSP partners or enable any CSP partner to resell.
caveats: Requires app to already be enable to transact

features.name: CSP private offers
features.description: ISVs create private offers as variants or wrappings of their apps for CSP resale. Define availability period, pricing, margins, and which CSP partners can access each offer.
caveats: ISVs can create multiple private offers with different terms for same app
Indirect CSP partner experience may differ based on partner portal implementation using APIs

features.name: CSP API support for indirect providers
features.description: All CSP functionality and private offers are API-enabled so that indirect providers can enable this capability in their own ordering systems and marketplaces for their resellers.
caveats: Indirect providers must implement the functionality in their own platforms

features.name: CSP direct bill partner self-service
features.description: CSP direct bill partners can use Partner Center to view private offers made available by ISVs, see available margins and pricing, and purchase offers on behalf of customers. Partners must be delegated admins and can then transfer licenses to customers.
caveats: Indirect CSP partners use different partner portals based on APIs; experience may vary

features.name: Per-site and custom pricing models
features.description: Future support for pricing models beyond per-user model including per-site license, one-time fee, and combinations of both. Currently in development and roadmap phase.
caveats: No set dates provided for delivery
Currently only per-user model is available

features.name: Appsource transact for Business Central apps
features.description: ISVs can enable their Business Central apps to be transactable on AppSource marketplace and sold through CSP reseller channel. Requires setting up entitlements and managing side-by-side scenarios for existing customers.
caveats: Existing customers require side-by-side setup to avoid locking them out
ISVs should test on separate test apps before moving existing customers to transact
Internal team usage and entitlements require careful configuration
